$sources: Each support's layer is a palette finish of Data/Matter/Palette.json: the entry and the finish the work's own image is laid in (the paint master for a canvas, a print and lustreware; the plate master for a daguerreotype), and for ware the finish of its undecorated faces.

The thickness of a sheet a work is made on: a photographic print or a stereograph's card, as mounted, about 0.3 mm (thin card; no measured caliper of the museum's facsimiles was read); a daguerreotype's plate, a silvered copper sheet, about 0.5 mm (no measured plate was read). Both are first values: neither is seen edge on at gallery distances, and each keeps its face clear of what it lies on.

A panel's paint is laid in the paint of its own finish (accent.oil-on-panel: the canvas's oil film under varnish, over a smooth ground); its board and cradle are Data/Art/Panel.json's. A Chinese painting or calligraphy mounted as a hanging scroll or a handscroll is laid in the ink on its silk or its paper (accent.ink-on-silk, accent.ink-on-paper); its mount's thickness is Data/Art/Scrolls.json's. Paper made as any other object (a print, a card, a book's page, a leaf) is the paper's own entry.

A tapestry is a weave about 3 mm thick: Morris & Co.'s high-warp tapestries, wool weft beaten down over a cotton warp (the Albion sheet's weave, Docs/Stages/albion.md; no caliper of the Attainment was read).
